version.changelog:
openclaw360 v0.1.11

- Added support for new backup-list trigger type: pre_restore.
- Enhanced backup-clean and backup-clean [--dry-run] CLI options for safer backup management.
- Updated documentation to reflect these options and usage.
- No changes to logic or behaviors outside of improved backup operations and command documentation.

llm.summary: This is a disclosed local security-scanner skill, with the main caveat that installation fetches executable code from GitHub.

dimensions.detail: The requested reads and writes mostly fit a local security tool. Reading OpenClaw Skill directories is purpose-aligned, though the permissions section could state the default and system scan paths earlier.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses pip from a pinned GitHub revision, or a virtualenv fallback. This is disclosed and user-run, but the executable implementation is outside the reviewed artifact and lacks artifact hash verification.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill tells the agent to invoke a local CLI only after user-requested security analysis or explicitly enabled protection mode; scan-skills reads Skill files in user-specified and documented OpenClaw Skill directories.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No sudo, background service, scheduled task, or auto-update is requested. The skill persists local config, identity keys, audit logs, backups, and potentially a fallback virtualenv.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The described capabilities are coherent with the purpose: prompt checks, tool-call checks, output DLP checks, skill scanning, local audit logs, and backup/restore.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, review the referenced GitHub source at the pinned revision or install it in an isolated virtual environment. Be aware it will process prompts, tool parameters, outputs, Skill files, audit logs, and local backups when you ask it to run security checks.
llm.findings:
[YR1] expected: The remote pip install is real and is the way the CLI is obtained; it is disclosed and pinned, but users must trust or review the external repository.
[T08] expected: The static-scan supply-chain warning is valid as a caution, but it does not show hidden or malicious behavior in the skill artifact.
[SDI-3] expected: The fallback virtualenv path is disclosed in install commands but not included in the later write-scope wording, so documentation should be tightened.
[SDI-4] expected: The data-handling section says data is stored under ~/.openclaw360/ while install code may live in ~/.openclaw360-venv; this is an install-artifact disclosure gap, not evidence of data exfiltration.
[PE2] unexpected: This appears to be a false positive: the referenced text says sudo is not required and no sudo command is present.
[SQP-3] expected: The language rule affects report localization and does not materially expand authority or data access.
